gaps.criterion: Reconciliation returns zero discrepancies after an erasure
gaps.gap: The reconciliation LOGIC is built and asserted in both directions that matter - zero discrepancies when every actionable surface is proved, and the skipped surface named when one is not - and it deliberately walks PLAN to PROOFS, because checking that every proof matches a surface always passes and would never catch the case that matters. A zero-row proof counts as a real proof, since nothing to erase is a valid outcome. What does not exist is the EXECUTION that produces those proofs: nothing runs the redactions, so reconcileErasure has only ever been given proofs a test constructed. The criterion says 'after an erasure', and no erasure can yet be performed - sdk-data-rights plan-executions and the local redaction statements are both unwritten. Closing it needs the execution to run the surfaces in erasureExecutionOrder, emit a proof per surface, and reconcile against a real run.

gaps.criterion: Certificate includes shred proofs for encrypted PII
gaps.gap: NOT BUILT, and it would have been dishonest to claim otherwise by adding a crypto_shred entry to the plan with nothing behind it. The ShredProof type carries an optional keyRef for a destroyed vault key, but no surface in LeadFlow currently uses crypto_shred as its method, because LeadFlow stores no encrypted PII: leads and users hold plaintext columns, and there is no envelope encryption and no vault key to destroy. So the criterion is unmeetable as stated until either PII is moved behind sdk-vault or the criterion is rescoped to the redaction proofs this schema can actually produce. Both are real options and the choice is a design decision rather than a coding one - which is why it is recorded here rather than resolved by inventing a key reference that points at nothing.

gaps.criterion: Residency is recorded for every person and pool
gaps.gap: NOT BUILT. sdk-data-rights publishes GET /api/data-rights/residency/:person_id and POST /api/data-rights/residency/touch, and nothing in LeadFlow calls either, so no residency is recorded for any person or pool. This was left rather than half-built because residency is only meaningful once there is somewhere to record it against - the touch call needs a person id from a live tenant, and no gateway is reachable here, so an implementation would be untestable beyond asserting that a stub was called. Closing it needs the touch on every capture and link, a read on the Contact 360 panel, and a reconciliation that a person with no residency record is a discrepancy rather than a blank.
